title: ...who write on clouds...
program_note:
This piece is inspired by the idea of clouds, in three different ways.  First, the music modulates from one “cloud” mode to another, each designed specifically for the harp.  Second, there is a program, and third a poem, each presented below.

Through swirling clouds we see glimpses of indistinct shapes, obliterated by the gradual coalescing of rain-drops into a spring rain.  The strengthening thunderstorm moves off quickly, leaving a distant residue of thunder and rain-drops.  Gradually, a ray of light shines through, almost too bright to look at, until filtered by a thinner bank of clouds.  The shapes earlier seen now emerge, becoming clearer and clearer until lit from behind by the setting sun.

Promise

Swear, you who are distant and near, you who write on paper with your ink, on clouds with your gaze, on canvas with your paint, swear never to betray, never once to slander the face of your dream — beautifully created — whether it be friendship, or faith in people or in your songs.

A dream! — you gave it life — the dream lives — once created it no longer belongs to us, as we no longer belong to ourselves!

Swear, especially you who write on clouds with your gaze — the clouds are changing shape — it is easy to blacken the clouds’ face of yesterday’s dream with unbelief.

Promise, please!  Promise this to life, promise me this!

Promise!

Elena Guro

translated from the Russian by Clarice Cloutier

...who write on clouds... was commissioned by and written for Grace Cloutier to perform at the Israel International Harp Competition.  It is approximately 7:45 in duration.
